record_notes.DCP-LETT-1131: Sunday at Shrewsbury, editorially dated October 31 by illness comparison with the Emma letter. Two missing Hooker notes from Thursday and Friday prompt the conditional Saturday visit, Sydenham phaeton and three train options. Two bad stomach days, now improved, and inability to leave before Wednesday are separate from intended travel. Raw MathML makes the dinner deadline 6½, not 612. Maldive flora is an explicitly conditional guess, not an observed distribution. No surviving prompt or completed visit is established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1133: Saturday at Down, editorial November 6: just received an unlocated cancellation note and praises the intended visit as friendship. He could not leave Shrewsbury before Thursday, and reached home last night; the body does not say he departed last night. Monday Kew farewell is conditional on health and only an hour, later specified noon. Will send science letter for the voyage; thanks Frances Henslow and congratulates completion of Flora Antarctica. Even a later sailing date would not justify another Down visit. Publication of the final Flora part is editorial context, not proof Darwin read it all.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1134: Monday, editorial November 8 following November 6: illness prevents the farewell meeting, including disappointment over the previous day. Darwin P1–4 says farewell and will write to Hooker in India; he does not promise to write from India. Emma contributes her own farewell P5–6, signed E. Darwin. XML sole-Darwin attribution must not turn Emma into answer voice. No surviving incoming prompt; prospective Kew meeting failed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1158: Composite Hooker letter headed February 20, ending March 16. P1–11 report cheetah/hawk hunting and infertility, river limits, elephant varieties and behavior, dogs/cattle/color/altitude, climate after deforestation, spiders/swallow migrations, kunkar and salts, coal, barberry and Vallisneria. Many facts are informant reports or conjectures, not all personal observations. Crocodile disappearance after total deforestation is prospective, contrary to the synopsis implication of completed extinction. P6 crocodile postscript was inserted with March 4 blue-ink section. P12–17 March 4 cover itinerary, Calcutta patrons, quoted Thomson geology, heart symptoms and uncertain future travel; Thomson quotation stays attributed. P18–21 March 8 revise the route away from Calcutta. P22–25 literal February 16 is corrected to March 16 from itinerary: only this final section acknowledges a missing Darwin letter received through Falconer just before leaving Mirzapore. Griffith journals are recommended but Hooker has not studied them. Borneo plans are prospective. Separate Darwin pencil scores have no demonstrated contemporary annotation date. Earlier cheetah inquiry 889 is an ongoing documented question, not proved sole immediate prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1174: May 10 explicitly answers the long Indian letter. P1 recognizes Hooker uncertainty about prior zoological knowledge; recommends Blyth, renews domestic-breed origins and bee questions, challenges the distinctive wild/domestic Bhil fertility claim, and discusses altitude asymmetry. It says plants where Hooker 1158 P5 discusses animals: preserve the mismatch rather than silently repairing Darwin. Maldive guess remains unanswered. P6 reports stomach trouble, boulder/admiralty work, microscope and barnacle sexual systems and theoretical interpretation; raw MathML is a ⅛-inch object glass, not 18 inches. Later 1851 taxonomy/discovery narrative remains editorial. P7 family and party news also acknowledges a separate unlocated packet from Frances Henslow; P8 scientific gossip does not establish attendance at the meetings; P9 answers Hooker chest symptoms. Supported reply to 1158 with added material and other channels acknowledged, no precise receipt time.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1193: July 24 Hooker acknowledges Darwin letter and specifically reacts to its barnacle sex finding, supporting 1174 as antecedent. He will prepare fuller answers from Hodgson, who has given him pamphlets for Darwin; this is not proof of Darwin receipt. Pallas recommendation is a question, not new Darwin knowledge by itself. P2 reports improved own health and Falconer recovering; service credit pursuit is not a completed administrative action. Next-mail promise is prospective. P4 signature dates main note July 24. P5 appended Darjeeling elevation announcement contains yesterday, but footnote 7 quotes a July 19 letter to his father reporting the same discovery last night; exact relative dating of this appended note is held. Later 1852 Everest discovery is unavailable in 1848. Mountain measurement is reported information with lacunae, not a silently corrected modern altitude.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1202: October 6 with supplied 1848 year: answers tiny note, Hooker freedom from heart pains, Hodgson pamphlets/Pallas, response to supplemental males and Falconer illness, a distinctive cluster matching 1193. Other expedition news came through Sir William and Frances Henslow; missing or unidentified letters remain separate inputs. Gratitude for pamphlets does not specify physical delivery or reading. Ross Voyage is explicitly finished and botanical summaries abstracted; September 17 completion is separately documented in footnote, not the date of this letter. Darwin does not yet identify the Falkland cattle-hunt author; later 1220 revelation cannot be imported. P4 describes new dissections, provisional more curious case withheld, homologies and proposed nomenclature reform; it does not describe the withheld case or prove successful reform. Reply link is supported, while Ross reading and other news extend beyond the tiny note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-889: Additional full rereading of July 11–12 1845 Darwin letter and enclosure: birth, Galapagos questions/results, seaweed correction, colonial discussions and theories, books read or sought, pollination, climate, Pacific flora/fauna, cheetah/silkworm questions, Forbes and visits, Irish yew. P4 explicitly pauses until tomorrow, so do not date entire body July 11. Enclosure asks collection counts/origins and contains Hooker pencil answers explained in footnotes; they are not Darwin prose. P8 is the earlier specific question whether domesticated cheetahs breed/copulate and which sex is affected. 1158 P1 answers the ongoing breeding question, but later oral/written reminders and its separate missing Darwin input prevent identifying 889 as sole immediate antecedent. Prior 1844–1846 reply relationships remain unchanged.
